chapter_theme: The chakra of the holy hall (திருஅம்பலச் சக்கரம்): diagrams of crossing lines and cells are filled with the five syllables na-ma-si-va-ya, Om, bindu and nada and the fifty-one letters, and the Dancer of the hall dwells in them. The five syllables are praised as the source of the elements, the Vedas and the Agamas, as what drives out the three impurities and ends birth, and are read letter by letter as Siva, Shakti, soul and bond; the chapter ends with drawn figures used for worldly rites of fixing, enchanting, driving away, killing and attracting.
structure_note: Construction and filling of the chakra (914 to 929); the letters, Om, bindu and nada in the chakra and the body (930 to 964); the five syllables praised and interpreted, with further grids (965 to 996, grids at 987 to 991 and 995); six rites with drawn figures (997 to 1002). Many verses are technical instructions whose layout can't be recovered from the words alone.

914.reading: The circle has twelve lines, and twelve more are set across them; the houses so formed number a hundred and twenty-one, and in one of those houses he himself arrives.
914.nuance: ஈராறு பத்தொன்று is taken as 121, the eleven by eleven cells that twelve lines each way make. Who arrives (எய்துவன்) is left unnamed; in context it is the Lord, or the worshipper's letter.

915.reading: The place where he dwells is his own letter; one letter with four makes the letters of his great name, the five letters set in the square, and the one who is the one within the one is Hara.
915.nuance: தன் எழுத்து (his own letter) is commonly taken as சி, the one that with four others makes நமசிவாய. நாற்கோணம் is the square of the diagram.

916.reading: Nothing is as rare as saying 'Hara Hara'; people don't know to say it; by saying it they become as the gods, and by saying it birth is cut off.
916.nuance: The plainest verse of the opening: the name alone, without diagram, is enough. அமரரும் ஆவர் can mean they become immortals or become like the gods.

917.reading: There are eight stations where my Lord dwells; in the eight, with one, six and fourteen, and bindu and nada joined and rising, the mantra was formed by the one of milk-sweet speech.
917.nuance: The numbers (one, two threes, two sevens) are not explained, and பான்மொழி may name the goddess 'of milk-sweet speech' or describe the mantra's sound.

918.reading: People don't know the means by which he stays joined with the good lady of the opening lotus; those who unite the letter that is let go with the letter not let go can guard the precious life.
918.nuance: விட்ட எழுத்து and விடாத எழுத்து are traditionally taken as the outgoing and the held breath, or the spoken and the unspoken syllable of the previous chapter's ajapa. கட்டவில்லாருயிர் is obscure; read here as கட்டு அவிழ் ஆருயிர், the life whose bond is loosed, or the precious life.

919.reading: The five syllables are seated as a temple; when this gross temple is passed, the subtle known as temple remains, and there he sits enshrined.
919.nuance: தூலம் and சூக்குமம் (gross and subtle) may mean the gross and subtle body or the spoken and inner forms of the mantra; ஆலயம் (temple) carries the verse in all four lines.

920.reading: This circle has six lines, within them lines making five, and the cells come to twenty-five; in one of these cells the letter A takes its place.
920.nuance: Six lines each way give five by five, twenty-five cells, the smaller grid filled in 921 to 924.

921.reading: Shakti is curved in the middle of MA, O curved around it, U split and raised; A is the head, SI the two eyes, NA and VA the good legs: so the figure is sought.
921.nuance: The letters seem to be shaped into a figure with head, eyes and legs, traditionally taken as the form of the Dancer drawn from the syllables. The way the letter shapes are combined can't be recovered from the words.

922.reading: Om, the pranava, is set in the middle and on both sides; in the central face is NAMASIVAYA, and SIVAYANAMA runs in the outer circle.
922.nuance: ஆடும் அவர் வாய் (the mouth of the one who dances) is obscure; it may tie the diagram to the Dancer of the hall.

923.reading: The mantra is examined in its rotations, SIVAYANAMA, MASIVAYANA, NAMASIVAYA, YANAMASIVA, VAYANAMASI, taken in order from SI.
923.nuance: The five rotations of the five syllables, each beginning on a different letter, fill the rows of the grid. The last line (தொட்டநதத் தடைவிலே) is obscure.

924.reading: In order, the fifty letters go two to a cell in the twenty-five cells; with KSHA, the last, placed at MA, all fifty-one letters are set.
924.nuance: Fifty-one is the count of the Sanskrit alphabet with க்ஷ added; the verse fits the whole alphabet into the five-syllable grid.

925.reading: The outer circle is set with 'Hara Hara', the circle within it with 'Hari Hari', the circle within that with the ajapa, and the lines become a trident.
925.nuance: அசபை is the unspoken mantra of the breath, subject of the previous chapter. அரிகரி may be Hari or a variant of Hara.

926.reading: At the trident's head Shakti appears, around it Om, in the space between its prongs the five letters appear, and this is also the way to reach the Lord of the banyan.
926.nuance: ஆலப்பதி may be the Lord under the banyan or a place; the reading of the figure depends on how the trident of 925 is drawn.

927.reading: That is A, I, U, E and O, five; they form circle upon circle of the chakra, and in the shared space between, our name swells.
927.nuance: நம் பேரே may be 'our name' or the syllable நம.

928.reading: What received the name is the root mantra; after it, the chakra stands set straight at the junction within the circle, and this is the nature of its form.
928.nuance: சோர்வுற்ற (wearied, slack) of the circle is obscure and may be corrupt.

929.reading: The Lord makes clear the working of the way this mantra is reached; wind, water, fire, earth and sky stood before the letters that are sounded.
929.nuance: முயலும் எழுத்துக்கு முன்னா may mean the elements came before the letters, or stand in front of them as their places in the diagram.

930.reading: Above the forty-eight letters set six and fourteen, above them bindu and nada; standing fierce and saying SIVAYANAMA, the three impurities cry out and leave.
930.nuance: The count (6 x 8, then 6 and 14) is not explained. கூப்பிட்டுப் போமே pictures the impurities fleeing with a cry; the claim that the mantra removes the three malams is plain whatever the numbers mean.

931.reading: The Lord is within her letter and the good lady within the Lord's letter; those who think of the two dwelling there in accord are the virtuous who know the meaning.
931.nuance: Tradition takes சி as Siva's letter and வ as Shakti's; the verse says only that each is within the other's.

932.reading: Set A, place ARA above it, set I, and it stands as a linga; set MA, and once the breath is seen rising above, it becomes a flame-tip sealed with 'thom'.
932.nuance: அரவு may be the letters ர or ஹ, or the serpent. தொம் may be a seed syllable. The verse shapes letters into a linga and then a flame.

933.reading: There is A, there is SA, everything is there; no one knows the purpose for which SA stands; for those who know the purpose of KA, SA is Shakti and Sadasiva.
933.nuance: அ, ச and க are not explained; they may be letters of a seed mantra, or அ and ச Siva and Shakti as in 957.

934.reading: By the five letters Nandi is seated; by the five letters the pancakshara is seated; the five letters make the letter-chakra, and within the five letters he is seated.
934.nuance: The circling of அஞ்செழுத்து in every line makes the Lord, the mantra and the diagram one thing.

935.reading: Many signs are told for seeing the Dancer; those who recite the first of the Dancer's letters stand as one in creed with him, and that is the sign for seeing the Dancer.
935.nuance: Which letter is first is not said: ந in the usual order, சி as the Lord's own letter, or Om.

936.reading: If one raises the fire within that direction and recites the letter NA within that direction, the Vedic one in that direction is made to dwell within that direction.
936.nuance: அத்திசை (that direction) opens every line; directions of the diagram are assigned to letters and deities, but which is meant is lost. மறையன் may be Brahma, the Vedic one, or 'the hidden one'.

937.reading: If one looks to the lady he himself gives, he gives and places her above; when one recites the MA he gave, it becomes a gem-light he has given.
937.nuance: கல்லொளி (light of stone, a gem's light) links this verse to the next. The grammar of who gives and who is placed is unclear.

938.reading: The north stood as gem-light, Indra stood as gem-light, and he showed the letter SI, which stood as gem-light, as gem-light.
938.nuance: Indra is usually the guardian of the east, not the north, so either the diagram's scheme differs or the line is disturbed.

939.reading: He himself stands as cool light with the seven qualities, as the Vedas with them; if one recites what becomes those qualities, he becomes the self-risen Vedic one.
939.nuance: எழுகுணம் may be 'seven qualities' or 'the rising quality'. The last line may mean the reciter or the Lord becomes the Vedic one.

940.reading: Births esteemed as those of the Vedic man are seen as such, but the Vedic man in whom the five letters have come to stand becomes those five letters himself.
940.nuance: One reading: the true மறையவன் is made by the five syllables dwelling in him, not by the birth people esteem. The first two lines are compressed and may only say the birth is held in honour.

941.reading: NA stands at the feet, MA at the navel, SI and VA are seen at the shoulders, and the light above is of the nature of YA.
941.nuance: The syllables are placed on the body from foot to crown. சீயுரு தோள் is unclear: சி may be at the chest or with வ at the shoulders.

942.reading: Nandi excelled in giving the six letters of that nature their fine nature; if one looks at them alike and filled with light, he stands spread through them.
942.nuance: இருமூன்று எழுத்து, six letters, is commonly Om with the five syllables. ஒவ்வியல், பவ்வியல் play on the letters ஒ and ப and are obscure.

943.reading: The mantra spreads to all lives; it is the boon-giving mantra; take it so it fits; it is the mantra that drives away surrounding enemies, the mantra that gives strength: raise it with Om.
943.nuance: சூழ்பகை (surrounding enmity) may be outward enemies or inner foes; both readings stand, and the chapter's closing rites (997 to 1002) show the outward sense was also in view.

944.reading: Raising the excellent Nandi with Om, raising the lamp that rises in the middle with NAM, raising with AAM: those who know that way saw the great hall and rejoiced.
944.nuance: மாமன்று is the great hall, the அம்பலம் of the chapter's title, here seen within. நாம், ஆம் may be syllables or words ('we', 'it is').

945.reading: Within the chakra the five letters are poured into the steps joined part by part; with the fifty-one letters within, the Supreme beyond stands joined to it.
945.nuance: பாகொன்றி and வார்த்திக்கும் are obscure; யாகொன்றி may be a misprint for ஆகொன்றி.

946.reading: With the supreme five letters set in the middle, further orders of the syllables are given, ending in the form VASI-MAYANAMA.
946.nuance: The strings (நவசிவ, மவயரசி, சியநம, வாசி மயநம) do not form the clean rotations of 923 and include a stray ர; they are likely corrupt.

947.reading: The elements match the letters, the colours match the letters; when the letters stand matched, he stands within those letters.
947.nuance: Each syllable is traditionally given an element and a colour; the verse doesn't list them.

948.reading: The chakra stands for the whole wide earth; Nandi, as a calf, drew milk from the good Lord of the land of maya who stands as the hall, and he is one whose way is to stand on the mountain.
948.nuance: The calf milking its mother is a common image for drawing grace by love. Who is the calf and who is milked is not certain, and குன்று may be Kailasa or a yogic height.

949.reading: Within this chakra are many qualities, five signs and the Dancer's five letters, and the dance stands within it.
949.nuance: The dance (கூத்து) of the hall is set inside the drawn diagram; the five signs are not named.

950.reading: Outside a line, on the line its head, in the curl U, fire around it, the bending stroke and horn, O, bindu and nada: this clear plan is the Siva mantra.
950.nuance: The verse names the strokes of the written letters (கால், கொம்பு, the curl and the dot) as parts of the drawn mantra; the figure itself can't be reconstructed.

951.reading: With A, U and SI in the middle, VA and the six joined with the breath, and with SI contemplating Siva, the Lord of O stands pleased.
951.nuance: A near-variant of 976 and 982. 'The six' (ஆறும்) is unexplained.

952.reading: Where all ceases, A arises; where it is reached, the true object is seen; that bright light which cut away anger, the true object, is a pill like gold with its dross removed.
952.nuance: குளிகை is the alchemist's pill that turns base metal to gold; the image makes the realised mantra a transforming pill. அற்ற இடம் may be the place where breath or thought stops.

953.reading: When A is sounded with U, the release that is U melts and mingles; how shall I tell the nature of my father, Nandi, who came into me as MA?
953.nuance: அ, உ, ம are the parts of Om; the verse moves from the syllable to the speaker's experience of the Lord within.

954.reading: What the people of this world know is letters on water; no one sees and knows the one letter in the sky; and those who know this letter do not perceive the letter in the flesh.
954.nuance: Writing on water is the stock image of what doesn't last. The last two lines can be read as a rebuke (even knowers miss the letter in the body) or as 'who knows this letter? they do not perceive it in the flesh'.

955.reading: At morning the letter is centred in the body, at evening the fifty letters are; with the root spoken by the Veda centred above, he gave release.
955.nuance: நடுவுற (being centred) in every line suggests stages of practice through the day; மூலம் may be the root mantra or the root centre.

956.reading: Below the navel is one good letter; sinners don't know its use; it can't be known even by painters; the Goddess and he shine there together.
956.nuance: ஓவியர் may be painters (it can't be drawn) or those who have ceased (renouncers). நாவி may be the navel or musk. The centre below the navel is traditionally the base of kundalini.

957.reading: The mantra Hara attained is A with SA; no one knows A with SA; once someone knows it, A with SA becomes the beginningless as well.
957.nuance: அவ்வொடு சவ்வு is unexplained: perhaps Siva and Shakti, or the syllables of a seed mantra. அதரன் may be அ(த்)து அரன் or a variant.

958.reading: One mantra, springing from the flower, rises within the navel; people perform the twilight rites without knowing it, worship at dusk, and go off making noise.
958.nuance: A rebuke of outer ritual: சந்தி (the twilight rite) done aloud without knowing the mantra that rises within. The flower (மலர்) is the inner lotus as tradition reads it.

959.reading: The mantra of worship gives direction; the mantras within the life are its supports; if one looks at the mantra within the flower without letting it go, the mantra within the life is a goad.
959.nuance: ஆதாரம் is the yogic support-centre or simply a base. The goad (அங்குசம்) anticipates 977.

960.reading: In the formless is the sky, where nada rises; in the swelling drum-shaped waist is the cherished bindu; joining in the middle of YA and SI, the true mantra wells up as it takes form.
960.nuance: துடியிடை (the drum-shaped middle) may be the waist of the body or of Shakti. The verse places nada above and bindu below.

961.reading: When bindu and nada join and meet the moon, nectar comes and wells up in the inner sky, and the mantra rising there becomes the oblation.
961.nuance: The moon is traditionally the centre at the head from which nectar flows in yoga. The fire rite is turned inward: the mantra itself is the oblation. அங்குதி is read as அங்கு உதி(த்த).

962.reading: Those who recite the six letters don't know them, nor recite the six as one and understand; for those who can utter it with no other letter, by one letter life can be won.
962.nuance: The six letters are commonly Om with the five syllables, and the one letter Om or சி. உயிர்பெறல் may be gaining life (long life) or gaining the soul's release.

963.reading: With the recited letters go the soul-letters, three fives; the first letters are said to be fifty-one; in the light-letters there are ten and three more; set down the nada letter and seek.
963.nuance: உயிர்க்கலை மூவைஞ்சு (fifteen) and ஐயிரு மூன்று may count vowels and other letter groups; the arithmetic is not clear.

964.reading: As nada rises spiralling from bindu, the mistress of bonds becomes sixteen kalas; she took the beautiful letter-form with breath as her body, and without end became the fifty-one.
964.nuance: பந்தத் தலைவி (mistress of bonds) is Shakti as the power that binds and releases. The sixteen kalas are traditionally the vowels or the moon's digits; the fifty-one are the letters.

965.reading: The fifty letters are all the Vedas and all the Agamas; once one knows what the fifty letters become, the fifty go and become the five letters.
965.nuance: The whole of scripture is reduced to its letters, and the letters to the five syllables. The verse recurs almost word for word as 2698.

966.reading: By the five letters he made the five elements, by them the many wombs of birth, by them he bears this wide world, and by them he stands seated.
966.nuance: யோனி is the kinds of birth, traditionally 84 lakh. The five syllables are made the instrument of creation and support.

967.reading: To one who, falling and rising, begins the holy name of the Transcendent and does not tire and give it up, the Lord comes to take away the grief of the deeds that cling, says the one with coiled locks.
967.nuance: வீழ்ந்தெழல் may be falling down in worship and rising, or falling and rising in life. The final line puts the promise in the Lord's own mouth.

968.reading: He stands as the food one eats and the medicine, endless time, learned hearing and song; while the gods in heaven long to worship his feet, he has become the five letters, beyond reckoning.
968.nuance: எண்ணின்று may be 'beyond count' or 'standing in thought'. The gods worship from afar what is near in the syllables.

969.reading: By the greatness of the five comes the wide world, by it the temple, by it the way of the virtuous one, and by working the five in their kinds one becomes the protector.
969.nuance: ஐந்து (the five) is in context the five syllables, but could be the five acts or elements. பாலன் may be the protector or a child (one guarded).

970.reading: As the root letter he is sky and beyond; as the water letter he bears the earth too; as the fine letter he is fire; and the letter that is life, the one-letter Lord, is bright light.
970.nuance: Each syllable is matched to an element; the verse's assignments don't plainly match the usual scheme (ந earth, ம water, சி fire, வ air, ய sky). வேரெழத்து looks like a misprint for வேரெழுத்து.

971.reading: The sound of the fourth letter is the world's form; within the fourth letter the world is contained; for those who can recite the fourth letter, it is the good path.
971.nuance: The fourth letter is commonly taken as வ, fourth in நமசிவாய and traditionally Shakti's letter; it may also be a number for another syllable.

972.reading: The bejewelled lady joined, entered my heart and loved there the word NAMASIVA; she holds the step that knows the fearful, she moved, and I cut away all other babble.
972.nuance: The verse recurs as 1115 with அயன்தனை for பயந்தனை and with the lady, not the speaker, cutting the babble (பெயர்ந்தனள், அறுத்தாளே). பயந்தனை ஓரும் is obscure.

973.reading: For those who stay saying the name NAMASIVA, the lady of the rule shines: the one woman who stays sweetly in the stomach and in the fire raises up the sheath of food.
973.nuance: ஆமம் (the stomach, or undigested food), அன்னமயம் (the food-sheath) and ஓமம் (the fire rite) suggest Shakti as the digestive fire that turns food into the body; this is a traditional reading.

974.reading: Knowing the liking of the supreme five letters as is fitting, while night and day come, she takes her place in the middle where the dance is danced and stands as the substance of the eight directions.
974.nuance: பட்ட பரிசே and பரமஞ் செழுத்ததின் are compressed. Night and day may be the two breaths; the middle, the central channel or the hall's centre.

975.reading: A is the soul, U the supreme and MA the impurity in the three-part word; SI is Siva, VA the form, and YA, one may say, is the soul.
975.nuance: Both Om and the five syllables are read as the Siddhanta categories. Tradition takes வ as Shakti, the Lord's form (வடிவம்) of grace. A is made the soul here, where Kural 1 makes A the image of the Lord.

976.reading: With NA, MA and SI in the middle, the two VAs joined with the breath, beginning with O and uttered once, the first Lord MA is within the mind.
976.nuance: 'The two VAs' and 'Lord MA' are unexplained; the verse is a near-doublet of 982 and close to 951.

977.reading: Five elephants live in the forest; for the five, the five letters are the goad; for those who can hold all five together, the First beyond the five can enter within.
977.nuance: The five elephants are the senses, though the verse doesn't name them. அஞ்சாதி ஆதி may be 'the First before the five' or 'the fearless First'; அகம் புகல் may be his entering the heart or their entering his.

978.reading: In the five kalas, beginning with A, the order beginning with NA is changed to begin with MA; for those who seek Nandi at the root and join with the Supreme Shakti, there is no ritual.
978.nuance: சந்திசெய்வார் plays on the twilight rite (சந்தி) and joining: the inner union replaces the outer rite. மூலம் is traditionally the base centre.

979.reading: SIVAYA, joined, becomes the abiding soul, the precious enjoyment and knowledge; the soul that has come to clarity goes on by these, grace settles in it, and becoming that Siva is release.
979.nuance: சிவாய without நம is traditionally the subtle form of the mantra, with the impurity (ம) and concealment (ந) dropped, as in the ninth tantra's subtle pancakshara.

980.reading: Once the truth of the five letters is known, the Supreme stays firm within the heart; there is no deceit and no ruin to the house; I declare that this is refuge.
980.nuance: அஞ்சுக (opening) may be 'fear' (imperative) or a form of அஞ்சு, five; மனை (house) may be the household or the body.

981.reading: Recited clearly in the heart, SIVAYA with A becomes Siva's form; those who can see SIVAYA with A clearly stayed in that clarity.
981.nuance: அவ்வே may be the letter அ added to சிவாய, or simply 'that'.

982.reading: With SI, VA and YA, and NA and MA sought in the middle, uttered once with O, the first Lord MA stands esteemed.
982.nuance: A near-doublet of 976, beginning from சி rather than ந.

983.reading: The acts sought in the five beginning with NA, the hard deeds contained in the five beginning with A: for those who can see clearly within the first SI, Sadasiva becomes their own First.
983.nuance: The two groups of five (from ந and from அ) may be the five syllables and the five vowels; the point is that seeing சி first frees from deeds.

984.reading: NAVA and SIVA become the soul and the Supreme; what lacks tapas is only tattva; those who search, at one with Siva, in devotion reached the clarity that they are what is called Siva.
984.nuance: நவம் is obscure: perhaps ந and ம (soul and bond), or 'the new'. The closing claim, that the seeker becomes Siva, is the Siddhanta goal of oneness without loss of the soul, as tradition reads it.

985.reading: Know by gathering the eight and the two; set Nandi whom you sought within knowledge, and the five who danced become kin there; seek it and know it clearly.
985.nuance: In Tamil numerals அ is 8 and உ is 2, so எட்டும் இரண்டும் is traditionally read as the letters அ and உ. The five who danced are the senses, now made kin.

986.reading: They don't know the eight and two well; the poor who don't know them miss that the eight and two, as six and four, are the step of the true path of Siddhanta.
986.nuance: இருமூன்று நான்கு (two threes and four, or six and four) is unexplained. சித்தாந்த சன்மார்க்கம் names the path explicitly.

987.reading: Draw eight lines across eight lines, set one letter of the Lord in the middle, place the forty-eight cells within the circle, and recite the five letters quickly.
987.nuance: Eight lines each way make seven by seven, forty-nine cells: the centre for the Lord's letter and forty-eight around it. சிட்டஞ்செழுத்து is read as the prescribed (சிட்ட) five letters.

988.reading: Danavas, the Sattars, the two Chatirars, with these three the Atravar and the rest, the other fifteen, bindu and nada and the host: this is the Siva chakra.
988.nuance: The names are classes of beings or letter groups placed in the cells; most can't be identified.

989.reading: The six of great penance who suffered and the Supreme; those who gave up the self say 'to the Transcendent, nama'; however many the eight ways of the Lord, I join them and speak, I know nothing else.
989.nuance: The first line is obscure. விகிர்தா நம (homage to the Transcendent) is the mantra form; the last line is the speaker's humility.

990.reading: Siva first, with the three and the five excelling; from them twelve, one with one; from them bindu and nada rising; first of the assembly is Sankara's own name.
990.nuance: The counts likely place deities or letters in the 49-cell grid of 987; சவை (assembly) may be the hall.

991.reading: Draw lines making the world as seed, set the sixteen kalas of the conch, then twelve in each kala from the first, and recite looking to the tenth, the Brahma rite.
991.nuance: நத்தார் கலை (kalas of the conch, or the moon's), உத்தாரம் and பத்தாம் பிரம சடங்கு are obscure.

992.reading: I found the honey within the lotus flower and rose with it; at the time of joining, going by the Lord's way that never perished of old, without losing the bond, it becomes 'nama'.
992.nuance: கண்டெடுந்தேன் puns on 'I found and took up' and 'honey'. பதிவழி may be the way of the Lord (பதி) or the settled way.

993.reading: The virtuous gods stand showering flowers and meditate on the mantra of the Lord's two feet; they draw near and, saying 'nama' with the name and holding it dear as their eyes, stand merged with it.
993.nuance: கண்என உன்னி (thinking of it as one's eye) means holding it most dear.

994.reading: The six letters are six mantras; for the six, four each, twenty-four, they say; in the Savitri there is one head-letter, and those who can discern it have ended their births.
994.nuance: The Savitri (Gayatri) has twenty-four syllables, which the verse matches to six times four. A variant reads சமயங்கள் for மந்திரங்கள்: the six letters would then be the six religious systems.

995.reading: Set eight cells in eight, fill the cells so that each joined one shows as eight, mark them and surround them with Om: for lives in bondage, Umapati is there.
995.nuance: The filling rule may be a magic square of eights. மட்டும் உயிர்கட்டு is obscure: perhaps 'for lives bound' or 'binding lives'.

996.reading: Those who take NA as first with A and hold it on the tongue, reaching within the eight beginning with A, and perceive U as first: on their crown the one who is first in U comes and stays.
996.nuance: The play is on letters as 'firsts'. உச்சி (crown) is the traditional head centre where the Lord is met.

997.reading: On a pipal board, set MA in one place, draw the figure on palm-leaf, smear dense wax over it and warm it in the flame, and fixing (stambhana) is seen.
997.nuance: 997 to 1002 give rites for worldly ends: தம்பனம் (fixing or paralysing), மோகனம் (enchanting), உச்சாடனம் (driving away), மாரணம் (killing) and வசியம் (attracting), traditionally among the six acts (ஷட்கர்மம்) of mantra practice. The verses state technique without comment, and many words of material and direction are uncertain.

998.reading: Set a board of karanai wood toward Yama's quarter, write 'death', set the letter MA in the eight, smear it with the five astringents and bury it by a hearth, and enchanting (mohana) follows.
998.nuance: கரண இரளி may be two woods or one; மரணம் இட்டு may be writing the word or the name of the target. Yama's quarter is the south.

999.reading: There in the north-west, in Ayyanar's shrine, on a board of palasa wood, smear it with bitter stuff, set the bindu, and place it so it doesn't rise: this is for driving away (uchchatana).
999.nuance: காங்கரு மேட்டில் is obscure; கடு may be a bitter or astringent paste.

1000.reading: At noon, in the fire-corner, spread the five astringents on a green palm-leaf and place it in a triple square in the old cremation ground, if one wants killing (marana) without fear.
1000.nuance: The fire-corner is the south-east. முச்சதுரம் may be a triple square or triangle. அச்சமற மேலோர் may mean 'the great, without fear' or 'without fear, over the enemy'. The verse gives the rite without approving or condemning it.

1001.reading: Smear yellow orpiment on the leaf, write the letters A and U, place it fittingly on a bilva board for attracting (vasiya), and recite eighty thousand times.
1001.nuance: எண்பதினாயிரம் (eighty thousand) is the count of recitations, as tradition reads it.

1002.reading: For Garuda, write U on the leaf, smear it with gold and silver, place it on a white naval-wood board facing west, and recite eight thousand times with the letters.
1002.nuance: எண்ணாக் கருடன் is obscure: perhaps a rite against poison invoking Garuda. Line 2 is corrupt in the source.

links.note: Both use the letter A to point beyond itself. The Kural makes A, first of letters, the image of the Primal Lord first in the world; Tirumular makes A the soul and gives the Supreme to U.
Both put a goad over 'the five'. In the Kural it is firmness of mind (உரன்) that guards the five; in Tirumular the five elephants in the forest are goaded by the five syllables.
Both make control of the five senses the way in: the Naladiyar's one who steers the craving of the five gates reaches release, Tirumular's one who holds the five together lets the First enter.
Both say deeds lose their hold on one devoted to the Lord: the Kural through his true praise, Tirumular through his name kept up without tiring, with the Lord coming to remove the grief of deeds.
Both define the Brahmin by something other than birth, if 940 is read that way: the Kural by kindness to all life, Tirumular by the five syllables dwelling in him.
The same verse recurs in the ninth tantra's gross pancakshara, with 'once the order of the fifty is known' for 'once what the fifty become is known'.
A near-doublet in the Bhairavi mantra chapter; there the lady herself departs and cuts away the babble, here the speaker does.
Both make the recited syllables drive out the impurities: here the three malams flee crying out, in 2712 sivaya removes all impurity and yields Siva-jnana yoga.
885 builds a ladder of one, two and three letters from the one letter that becomes the world; 962 says the six letters must be recited as one, and that by one letter life is won.
Both use the alchemist's pill (குளிகை) that makes gold: here the realised true object is the pill like purified gold, in 2709 sivayanama is the pill that turns the body's cage to gold.
Both move the temple inward: 1823 makes the body a shrine and the heart the great temple, 919 makes the five syllables and the subtle within the temple where the Lord sits.
958 mocks those who perform the twilight rite without knowing the mantra within; 978 says those who join with Shakti at the root need no rite at all.
Near-doublets: the same breath-joined recitation with O, ending on 'the first Lord MA', one starting from NA and one from SI.

198 sends those who say 'kill, strike' bound to hell; 1000 gives a rite for killing by mantra and diagram. The conflict holds if 1000 is read as offering the rite for use; read as a catalogue of what mantra can do, it is a report, not an endorsement.

916 repeats அரகர என்ன four times: no one says it, saying it they become gods (அமரரும் ஆவர்), and birth is cut off (அறும்பிறப்பு). 2716, in the subtle-pancakshara chapter, has the same frame with சிவசிவ: evil-doers don't say it, saying it ends evil deeds, they become gods (தேவரும் ஆவர்) and reach Siva's state. The two are one verse-form far apart, with the name changed and the reward moved from ending birth to சிவகதி.

Kural 10 says only those who reach the Lord's feet swim the great sea of births (பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல் நீந்துவர்). 916 names a means for the same end: merely saying அரகர cuts off birth (அறும்பிறப்பு), yet people don't know to say it. The Kural leaves the way of reaching unstated; the Tirumanthiram makes it the spoken name.

Both verses turn on the pair அவ்வு and சவ்வு and on no one knowing it: 933 says no one knows what ச stands for, and to those who know, ச is Shakti and Sadasiva; 957 says the mantra அவ்வொடு சவ்வு is known to no one (ஆரும் அறிகிலர), and once known it becomes the beginningless (அனாதி). Read together, the two show the same seed pair glossed once as Shakti with Sadasiva and once as the beginningless.

888 in the ajapa chapter says the dance is the single letter, the one letter (தாண்டவமான தனியெழுத்து ஓரெழுத்து). 935 turns that into practice: of the many signs for seeing the Dancer, reciting the first of the Dancer's letters (கூத்தன் எழுத்தின் முதலெழுத்து) makes one stand at one with him, and that is the sign. The identity of dance and letter becomes the way to see the Dancer.

941 places the five letters on the body: ந at the feet, ம at the navel, சி and வ at the shoulders, ய as the light above. 2701 places them elsewhere: mouth, throat, heart, navel, linga, up to the crown (இருமத்தகம்). Both map the syllables onto the body from low to high, but only the navel is shared, so the book carries more than one bodily scheme for the same mantra.

A near-repeat: 951 has அ, உ, சி in the middle and வ with the six joined with the breath (வளியுடன் கூடி), and the Lord of ஓ pleased; 976 has ந, ம, சி in the middle, the two வ joined with the breath, begun with ஓ and uttered once, and the Lord ம in the mind. The shared frame (நடுவாய், வளியுடன் கூடி, ஓகார) with different letters shows the formula reworked within the chapter.

954 says what the people of the world know is writing on water (நீரில் எழுத்து), and no one sees the one letter in the sky. 64 says that even countless crores of Agamas are writing on water (நீர்மேல் எழுத்தே) if one doesn't know what the Lord declared. Both use the image for knowledge that misses its one point, and 954 names that point as a single letter.

958 says a mantra rises in the navel, and people perform the twilight rite (சந்திசெய்யாநிற்பர்) without knowing it, worship at dusk and leave noisily. 2703 says at the times of sun and moon no one knows the fitting mantra (ஆயுறு மந்திரம் ஆரும் அறிகிலார்), but one may recite the five letters with the mouth. Both judge the timed rites by the mantra their performers miss; 2703 adds a plain remedy.

959 says the mantra within the life is a goad (ஆவிக்குள் மந்திரம் அங்குசமாமே) when one looks to it without letting go; 977 makes the five letters the goad (அங்குசம்) for the five elephants living in the forest. The goad is the same in both; 977 names what it drives, the five, and 959 places it inside the breath-life.

962 says those who recite the six letters don't know them, and for those who can utter it without another letter, life can be won by one letter (ஓரெழுத்தாலே உயிர்பெறலாமே). 2720 says though one recites the Vedas, limbs and Agamas, what is ours is in one letter (எழுத்து ஒன்றில்), and mastering it reaches the farther shore. Both reduce the recited many to one letter, and 2720 sets the whole of scripture against it.

965 says the fifty letters are all the Vedas and Agamas, and once known they become the five letters (ஐம்பது எழுத்தும்போய் அஞ்செழுத்தாமே). Thiruppugazh 1326 names Siva as the three-eyed light who teaches the four Vedas in the five letters (ஐந்தெழுத்ததனில் நான்மறை உணர்த்து). Both hold the Vedas within the five letters, the song in passing within Murugan's praise.

885 says by one letter he became everything in the world (ஓரெழுத்தாலே உலகெங்கும் தானாகி), then two, three and the great letter. 966 gives the same work to the five letters: by them he made the five elements, the many wombs, and bears the wide world (அஞ்செழுத்தால் இவ் அகலிடம் தாங்கினன்). Read together, the letter as the stuff of creation runs from the one letter to the five.

975 reads the letters as categories: சி is Siva, வ the form, ய the soul, ம impurity. 2710 lists Siva, Shakti, the soul, choking impurity and maya (சிவன்சத்தி சீவன் செறுமல மாயை) and says when the bonds go the soul joins Siva with Shakti. 2710 gives the same five without naming letters, which supports reading 975's வடிவம் as Shakti and makes clear what the letter key is for: separating the bonds from the soul.

980 says once the truth of the five letters is known the Supreme stands in the heart, there is no deceit or ruin to the house, and declares this the refuge (தஞ்சம் இதுவென்று). 2702 says when the soul leaves its instruments and death lays hand on it, the five letters bring shelter (அரணம் கைகூட்டுவது அஞ்செழுத்தாமே). The same protection is claimed for life in the house and for the hour of death.

981 says சிவாய with அ, recited clearly in the heart, becomes Siva's form. 2712 says that when the impurity named நம is removed and that beginning left, what one chants is சிவாய, the truth free of impurity (சிவாயமலமற்ற உண்மை). 2712 explains why 981 recites சிவாய without நம: the dropped syllables are the bond.

984 says those who search, at one with Siva, reach the clarity that they are what is called Siva (சிவம்என்பது தானாம்), and that what lacks tapas is only tattva. 2393 names that state as the goal of both systems: becoming Siva is Vedanta and Siddhanta (சிவமாதல் வேதாந்த சித்தாந்தமாகும்), and apart from it each is in vain. 2393 sets 984's claim at the head of the doctrine.

977 makes the five letters a goad for the five elephants and promises the First to those who can hold all five together (தடுக்கவல்லார்). 985, after setting Nandi within knowledge, says the five who danced become kin there (ஆடிய ஐவரும் அங்கு உறவு ஆவார்கள்). The same five are first restrained by force, then made kin once Nandi is within, which qualifies the restraint as a stage.

994 says the six letters are six mantras, matched to the twenty-four of the Savitri, whose one head-letter, if discerned, ends birth. Thiruppugazh 1326 ends with the Brahmins of the six letters (ஆறெழுத்து அந்தணர்) praising Murugan's feet at Eragam. Both tie a six-letter mantra to the Brahmin; in 994 it is measured against the Savitri, in the song it has become the Brahmin's own mark.

source_issues: 946: the syllable strings (மவயரசி, வாசி மயநம) don't form clean rotations of the five syllables and include a stray ர; likely corrupt.
956: line 3 has a stray backslash (அறியவொண் ணாத\து); read as அறியவொண்ணாதது.
1002: line 2 is corrupt (பொனefனாளிf), with Latin letters in the Tamil.
970: வேரெழத்து looks like a misprint for வேரெழுத்து.
945: யாகொன்றி may be a misprint for ஆகொன்றி.
994: a variant reads சமயங்கள் for மந்திரங்கள், changing six mantras into six religious systems.
972 recurs as 1115 with different words (அயன்தனை for பயந்தனை, பெயர்ந்தனள் and அறுத்தாளே for பெயர்ந்தனன் and அறுத்தேனே), so the speaker of the last line differs between the copies.
938: Indra is set with the north, though he is usually guardian of the east; the scheme or the line may be disturbed.
